content:
maya: Heads-up: saw a partner spike this morning that hit per-key burst but not org quota. Their jobs retried and caused a cascade.

dan: Which partner? any idea why only key-level triggered?

maya: partner-service-prod. They use an internal service account key for batched exports, so requests come from one key but many orgs behind it. We currently apply per-key burst windows without checking service-account flag.

priya: Hmm. This is the exact scenario we chatted about — internal keys that represent multiplexed downstream customers. Should we treat service account keys as "grouped" and apply per-org quotas downstream?

alex: We have two levers: 1) strict per-key burst (current), 2) per-org enforcement by inspecting header metadata (we already pass x-org-id).

jamie: UX question: if we add a console toggle to exempt "internal service" keys from per-key bursts and instead route them through per-org enforcement, ops needs visibility. We should surface which orgs are being affected and the aggregated rate.

maya: Agreed. Also need audit trail for overrides. Compliance wants an approval flow for manual key-level lifts.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2025-678, alert threshold tripped for partner-service-prod key at 04:12 UTC. Paging oncall.

dan: Quick mitigation: can we auto-throttle the key with a progressive slowdown (500ms, 1s, 2s) rather than hard reject? That would keep jobs alive and lower retry storms.

priya: Technically doable — our token bucket supports dynamic refill. But slowdowns interact with SLOs for latency-sensitive routes. We need route-level policy exceptions.

alex: Proposal: add a key metadata flag `service_type: multiplex` and a console workflow to set that. Runtime policy: if multiplex && org header present, split quota logic: evaluate per-org quota first, then per-key aggregate cap. Also add a grace buffer of X tokens per minute for short ramps.

maya: Sounds good. For UX: make default off, require two approvers for enabling, log who toggled and show a diff of recent rate/usage in the modal.

jamie: Can we also emit telemetry events so Optimize can recommend quantization/batching if cost rises because of these keys? Need a new metric: `key.multiplex.org_count` and `key.multiplex.peak_concurrency`.

priya: I'll add metrics. We'll tag traces with org-id and key-id for aggregation. Careful about PII — strip user ids.

compliance-bot: Note: any manual override must generate an approval record and retention 7 years for partner SLAs.

dan: Implementation plan: (1) API: key metadata flag + console toggle with 2-approver workflow, (2) runtime policy change to route to per-org logic if flag set, (3) progressive throttling as soft-fallback, (4) telemetry events & Optimize hook, (5) audit retention.

maya: Timeline?

alex: Can do a beta in 2 weeks if we scope to only routing + telemetry. Approvals modal + retention next sprint.

jamie: I'll design the modal and the console table row showing "multiplex key" with org_count and recent peak.

priya: I'll prototype metrics and a rollout alarm that triggers when org_count > 50 for a key.

dan: I'll implement the runtime policy and progressive throttle.

maya: Great. For immediate incident, I've applied a temporary soft-throttle to partner-service-prod (30s cooldown). Monitoring shows retries declined.

ops-bot: Incident #INC-2025-678 updated: temporary soft-throttle applied by maya.

alex: One more: we need clear docs for partners about using service keys vs per-org keys. Devex can add a migration guide.

maya: Thanks all — follow-ups: @jamie design mock, @dan runtime PR, @priya metrics PR. We'll sync tomorrow 10am PT. :thumbsup:
